## TL;DR - Agreement signed on 23 December 2020 - Effective January 1, 2024 - Old frontier workers: exemption of €7,500 - New frontier workers: deductible of €10,000
## Key facts - Agreement: December 23, 2020 - Entry into force: 1 January 2024 - Italian ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Old cross-border commuters: already such before 17 July 2023 - Transitional regime: 2024–2033 - New cross-border commuters: €10,000 deductible - 730: panel G, section III - IRPEF 2026: 23% up to €28,000; 33% €28'001–€50'000; 43% more
The New Cross-border Workers Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020, which came into force on 1 January 2024. The Italian ratification is Law 83 of 13 June 2023. For cross-border workers who live in Italy and work in the Canton of Ticino, the sequence of dates is the starting point of the 2026 calculation. Anyone looking for the new 2026 tax agreement must therefore start from the correct date: the agreement does not come into force in 2026, but from 1 January 2024.
The first check concerns the category. An old cross-border worker is someone who was already such before 17 July 2023. The exemption of €7,500 and the transitional regime 2024–2033 apply to this category. For new cross-border commuters the deductible is €10,000. In the focus on a single cross-border worker, this is the first separation to report before moving on to the declaration data. The transitional regime and the 2026 rates are two different pieces of information and must be noted separately.
### The rules to read together
Withholding tax on cross-border workers' income is withheld only in Switzerland, not in both countries. Italy avoids double taxation through tax credit. In 730, the credit for foreign taxes must be indicated in table G, section III; the CE framework belongs to the PF Income Model and should not be treated as a 730 framework.
From 2026 the Italian IRPEF is 23% up to €28,000, 33% between €28,001 and €50,000 and 43% over €50,000, according to Law 199/2025, art. 1, paragraph 3. For incomes 2024–2025 the reported rates are 23%, 35% and 43%. The comparison avoids applying the previous intermediate range to 2026.
The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland was signed on 9 March 1976. Switzerland is not part of the EU or the EEA. Tax rates, including withholding tax, derive from federal and cantonal laws: at federal level they are administered by the AFC/ESTV, while in the cantons they are the responsibility of the respective tax administrations. The first line of the checklist for a single border worker is the date of July 17, 2023, not the final balance of the paycheck. The date is used to choose between the old and new regime; the year 2026 is instead used to read the indicated personal income tax rates. Keeping the two steps separate reduces the risk of using the wrong excess.
### Two hypothetical scenarios
A border crossing already in place before 17 July 2023 falls under the old border crossing scenario: the exemption is €7,500 and the transitional regime covers the period 2024–2033. A frontier worker who is among the new ones applies the excess of €10,000. These are generic scenarios, without adding names, employers or places: the data to be verified is the temporal condition.
| Scenario | Data to be isolated | |---|---| | Old border | Before 17 July 2023; exemption €7,500; transitional 2024–2033 | | New frontier | Deductible €10,000 | | Earned income | Tax at source only in Switzerland; credit in Italy |
Comparison with net requires a second level. The Swiss percentages are not IRPEF rates: AVS/AI/IPG is 5.3% borne by the employee; AD/AC is 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148'200; LAINF is between 0.7% and 1.5%; LPP is between 7% and 18% by age group, from the 25th year. When the G-permitted reader compares disposable income, these items should be kept separate from the tax credit.
LAMal also remains on a different level: it is health insurance, G border workers have the right of option and the deductibles for adults indicated are between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500. It is not a health tax and should not be confused with the tax at source.
In the comparison of rates, the intermediate range goes from 35% indicated for 2024–2025 incomes to 33% from 2026. 23% remain in the range up to €28,000 and 43% over €50,000. To line up taxable, credit and withholding, you can use the calcolatore fiscale. Its use only makes sense after classifying the scheme: no numerical result can replace the verification of the date and the declarative framework. The transition from rule to form can be managed with a short checklist. The goal is not to mix status, fiscal year, and contributory items.
### Operational checklist for the single border crossing
1. Set the reference date. Check if you were already a border worker before 17 July 2023. If yes, it registers the exemption of €7,500 and the transitional regime 2024–2033; for new frontier workers it registers the deductible of €10,000.
2. Separate the withholding from the credit. Border workers' earned income is subject to tax at source only in Switzerland. In the Italian passage, the tax credit serves to avoid double taxation.
3. Choose the correct frame. In 730 he indicates the credit for foreign taxes in box G, section III. If you use the PF Income Model, the CE frame is the reference of the model: do not transfer it to the 730.
4. Apply the right year rates. For 2026 use 23% up to €28'000, 33% between €28'001 and €50,000 and 43% over €50,000. For 2024–2025 incomes, it retains the comparison of 23%, 35% and 43%.
5. Keep the other items separate. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP are Swiss contributions with the indicated rates; LAMal is health insurance. Do not turn these items into a tax at source.
Tax rates should not be attributed to social security or statistical institutions. Federal and cantonal laws establish them; at the federal level the administration indicated is AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations also operate. This distinction avoids looking for the calculation at the wrong institution.
Before closing the file, check that the chosen category, the deductible or exemption and the framework of the declaration are consistent with each other. After ordering this data, go to dichiarazione dei redditi.

## TL;DR - Checks from October 19 to 25, 2026 - Mobile and semi-stationary speed cameras in various locations - Areas frequented by Italian cross-border commuters are also affected
## Key facts - Who → Cantonal Police and municipal police forces - When → from Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25, 2026 - Where → locations in Canton Ticino - Objective → prevent accidents and raise awareness of compliance with speed limits - Motorway network → excluded from the advance notice
From Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Cantonal Police, together with the municipal police forces, will conduct new speed checks on the roads of Canton Ticino. The published list concerns checks using mobile and semi-stationary radar units in numerous locations throughout the region.
The notice also concerns the routes used daily by Italian cross-border commuters traveling to work across the border, with checks planned in various areas. The locations listed include Stabio, Morbio Inferiore, Balerna, Lugano, Agno, Bioggio and Locarno. The notice also indicates checkpoints in the districts of Lugano, Mendrisio and Locarno.
The municipal police forces list Bellinzona, Cadenazzo, Carasso, Giubiasco, Lumino, Preonzo and Sementina. The list also includes Arcegno, Gerra Gambarogno, Locarno, Losone, Minusio, Orselina, Riazzino, Tegna, Verscio and Vogorno. Another group comprises Agno, Bioggio, Canobbio, Gravesano, Loreto, Lugano, Manno, Melide, Molino Nuovo and Sorengo. For the Cantonal Police, Capolago and Riva San Vitale are listed.
### The purpose of the checks
The checks aim to prevent road accidents and raise motorists’ awareness of compliance with speed limits. The Cantonal Police reminds motorists that excessive speed is one of the main causes of accidents, which can have very serious or fatal consequences.
In addition to mobile radar units, semi-stationary checkpoints are planned in four locations during the week. The published list does not include checks conducted using unmarked cars and laser guns, which are used to combat serious violations of the Federal Road Traffic Act. ## The practical meaning for those crossing the border
For an Italian cross-border commuter, the notice should be read as advance information about the locations where checks will be carried out during the week of October 19 to 25. It is not, however, a list of all the ways in which the cantonal police may check speed. The source in fact distinguishes between announced checks and checks that remain outside the communication.
| Method | What the source communicates | |---|---| | Mobile speed cameras | They are planned in numerous locations from October 19 to 25 | | Semi-stationary units | They are planned in four locations | | Unmarked cars and laser guns | They are not included in the published list | | Motorway network | The advance notice does not cover these checks | | Extraordinary checks | They may be carried out without announcement |
### The list does not rule out other checks
The distinction is relevant for those who cross the border to get to work every day. If a location is listed, the commuter knows that it falls within the schedule communicated for that week. If a location does not appear, however, this does not mean that every form of check is excluded: the cantonal police retain the authority to order unannounced extraordinary checks when necessary to crack down on serious violations and ensure the safety of road users.
The same applies to unmarked cars and laser guns. The source specifies that these tools are not included in the list and are used against serious violations of the Federal Act on Road Traffic. For the cross-border commuter, therefore, the absence of a reported mobile speed-camera location does not mean that every possible check is absent.
There is also a clarification about the motorway network: the advance notice does not cover it, following the negative opinion issued by the Federal Roads Office, USTRA. The cantonal police also warn that the scheduled checks may not be carried out due to operational requirements or technical problems. The list should therefore be considered an announced plan, not a guarantee that every location will be active.
The cantonal police therefore urge people to observe speed limits even when no speed cameras are present, in order to protect their own safety and that of other road users. ## A practical sequence for the week
1. **Set the period.** The notice concerns exclusively the week from Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25, 2026. The cross-border commuter must therefore link the information to journeys falling within these dates.
2. Compare the locations. The list of municipal police forces includes Bellinzona, Cadenazzo, Carasso, Giubiasco, Lumino, Preonzo, Sementina, Arcegno, Gerra Gambarogno, Locarno, Losone, Minusio, Orselina, Riazzino, Tegna, Verscio and Vogorno. Agno, Bioggio, Canobbio, Gravesano, Loreto, Lugano, Manno, Melide, Molino Nuovo and Sorengo are also indicated, as are Besazio, Morbio Inferiore, Salorino, San Pietro and Stabio. For the cantonal police, Capolago and Riva San Vitale appear.
3. Consider both types announced. The week includes both mobile radar checks and semi-stationary positions. Semi-stationary positions are planned in four locations, while the notice provides no further details here about the individual positions.
4. Do not limit yourself to the list. Unmarked cars and checks with laser guns are not included in the communication. Extraordinary checks may also be ordered without notice when the cantonal police deem them necessary.
5. Maintain the limit throughout the journey. The recommendation also applies when no radar is indicated. Moreover, the actual presence of scheduled checks may change due to service requirements or technical problems.
For anyone crossing Canton Ticino every day, the most practical procedure is therefore to identify the period and locations concerned, distinguish between announced and unannounced checks, and not base their conduct solely on the presence of a checkpoint. The invitation from the cantonal police is addressed to all motorists and concerns their own safety and that of other road users.

item.description: Two minors aged 17 and 14 arrested in the act A 75-year-old pensioner falls but is not injured The stolen goods are recovered and returned Location: square
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two minors aged 17 and 14 arrested in the act - A 75-year-old pensioner falls, but is not injured - The stolen goods are recovered and returned
## Key facts - Location: Piazza Giovanni XXIII, in front of the station - Charge: theft with snatching - Minors: 17 and 14 years old - Presumed third young man: still to be identified - Stolen goods: a carton of cigarettes - Outcome: taken to the «Cesare Beccaria» First Reception Centre in Milan
### The apprehension after the snatching
The Carabinieri of the Operational and Radio-Mobile Unit of the Gallarate Company arrested two boys, aged 17 and 14, in the act. Both are accused of snatching something from a 75-year-old pensioner.
The incident took place in front of the railway station, in Piazza Giovanni XXIII. According to the officers’ reconstruction, this is the area where the intervention leading to the apprehension of the two minors took place.
The Carabinieri’s reconstruction indicates that the two boys allegedly acted with a third young man. The alleged accomplice is therefore part of the reconstruction of what happened, but his identity has yet to be established.
The group allegedly approached the elderly man and snatched from his hand a bag containing a carton of cigarettes. The carton had been purchased shortly beforehand at a tobacconist’s in the area.
The third young man is described as still being in the process of identification, while the two boys were apprehended in the act. The charge reported by the officers remains theft with snatching against the pensioner. ## The fall and the escape
### The patrol's intervention
During the snatching, the pensioner ended up on the ground, but the Carabinieri reported that the 75-year-old remained unharmed.
Immediately after the incident, the three youths fled on foot. For two of them, however, the escape did not last long: a Carabinieri patrol, passing through the area, allegedly witnessed the scene.
The patrol was engaged in the usual area-monitoring services. As they passed through the station area, the officers allegedly saw what was happening and managed to quickly detain the two minors.
In the report provided by the Carabinieri, the patrol's passage through the area and direct sight of the scene preceded the detention of the two youths. The intervention therefore unfolded while the officers were already engaged in ordinary area-monitoring duties.
The third youth, on the other hand, managed to get away. The reported sequence thus distinguishes the two detained minors from the alleged accomplice who remains to be identified, while the group's departure is described as having occurred on foot.
The sequence unfolded in the area in front of the station: after the snatching, the three moved away and the patrol passing by quickly detained two of them. Although he fell, the pensioner did not suffer injuries, according to what the officers reported. ## The stolen goods and what followed
### The checks still underway
The carton of cigarettes was recovered and returned to the pensioner. The stolen goods mentioned in the reconstruction therefore returned to the 75-year-old after the checks carried out by the Carabinieri.
The two boys were taken to the «Cesare Beccaria» First Reception Center in Milan after being placed at the disposal of the juvenile judicial authorities.
For the third alleged accomplice, what follows is different: the youth managed to get away and still has to be identified. Meanwhile, the Carabinieri's investigations continue to clarify his identity and his role in the incident.
The checks also include analysis of images from the municipal video-surveillance systems. The cameras considered by investigators cover the station area, where the snatching against the pensioner took place.
The follow-up indicated by the source therefore develops on two distinct fronts. On the one hand, the two minors have already been placed at the disposal of the juvenile judicial authorities and taken to Milan. On the other, investigations remain open into the youth who is said to have managed to flee.
The analysis of the municipal video surveillance concerns precisely the station area and accompanies the search for the third alleged accomplice. The recovered carton, on the other hand, was returned to the pensioner.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/buttano-a-terra-un-75enne-per-rubargli-una-stecca-di-sigarette-due-minori-fermati-dai-carabinieri-a-gallarate/2711179/)*

item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - AIC Lombardia in Varese from October 23 to 25 - Information desk and gluten-free refreshments at the Estensi Gardens - About 450 children at the Pulciniadi
## Key facts - Who → AIC Lombardia APS - When → from October 23 to 25 - Events → Varese CityRun and Pulciniadi - Desk → Giardini Estensi - Pulciniadi → approximately 450 children from preschools in Varese and the province
Between October 23 and 25, AIC Lombardia APS will propose two initiatives in Varese to promote awareness of celiac disease and inclusion: the Sport Project at Varese CityRun and an activity at Pulciniadi, with the participation of approximately 450 children from preschools in Varese and the province.
### Two initiatives in Varese
The proposal combines support for people with celiac disease during a sporting event with an educational activity aimed at young children. For CityRun, AIC Lombardia will be at Giardini Estensi with an information desk. At Pulciniadi, instead, it will offer a path to learning about celiac disease built around a fairy tale and materials designed for a child audience.
The association's initiative therefore unfolds on two distinct levels, but linked by the same objective: making inclusion more concrete. On the one hand, there is attention to the needs of athletes who must follow a gluten-free diet; on the other, there is work with children, who are called upon to better understand the needs of their classmates with celiac disease and the value of respecting differences.
The presence in Varese concerns not only the dissemination of information. The program combines a service intended to support participation in the sporting event with an educational moment in preschools. In this way, AIC Lombardia brings the issue of celiac disease into two places of collective life, sport and school, without separating it from food safety and social inclusion.
The sporting component will focus on contact with those who want to learn more about celiac disease and on the needs of athletes with celiac disease. The one at Pulciniadi, on the other hand, will be aimed at children, using language appropriate to their age. This is the structure of the two initiatives announced by the association for the days from October 23 to 25. ## The CityRun and support for athletes
At the Varese CityRun, AIC Lombardia will be present at the Estensi Gardens with an information desk. It will be the place to turn to for more information about issues related to celiac disease and the needs of people who must follow a gluten-free diet.
The presence will not be solely informational. Thanks to the Progetto Sport, athletes with celiac disease will be able to reserve refreshment bags with gluten-free products. The source specifies that the bags may also contain products from local businesses, an element that connects the association's service to the local reality of the event.
The refreshments are intended to allow everyone to take part in the CityRun with greater peace of mind and with the necessary attention to food safety. For those who must follow a gluten-free diet, the organization of a dedicated area and the possibility of reserving a specific bag accompany participation in the event.
### An information desk, a service for participation
The desk at the Estensi Gardens will offer an opportunity to learn more about aspects related to celiac disease, while the Progetto Sport will add a concrete response to the needs of athletes with celiac disease. They are two different functions of the same presence: on the one hand, information; on the other, refreshments with gluten-free products.
With this presence, AIC Lombardia aims to ensure that sporting events take into account the needs of people with celiac disease and are accessible to everyone. Participation in the Varese CityRun is thus accompanied by the promotion of a sports culture open to everyone, with a service based on food safety and attention to those who follow a gluten-free diet.
For athletes with celiac disease, the project offers the possibility of reserving refreshment bags. The products may also come from local businesses. The desk, on the other hand, will be intended for those who wish to learn more about celiac disease during the association's presence at the Estensi Gardens. ## Pulciniadi, fairy tales and educational materials
Approximately 450 children from preschools in Varese and the province will take part in movement, play and inclusion activities. AIC Lombardia will bring Ciccio il Riccio to them, the protagonist of a fairy tale designed to accompany them in discovering celiac disease.
The story is written in simple language suited to their age. This choice makes it possible to address the topic of celiac disease through a narrative tool aimed at younger children, while maintaining the connection with the themes of inclusion and respect for differences indicated by the association.
### From the fairy tale to the school program
Alongside Ciccio il Riccio’s fairy tale, AIC Lombardia provides other educational materials free of charge to schools participating in «Non solo glutine…». The training program, carried out with the local ATSs, is aimed at school staff.
The connection between the Pulciniadi and the school context broadens the meaning of the day beyond play. Through this initiative, children can better understand the needs of their classmates with celiac disease and, more generally, the value of respecting differences. The fairy tale thus offers age-appropriate language to bring them closer to learning about celiac disease.
Participation in the Pulciniadi complements support for athletes with celiac disease with educational work aimed at younger generations. For AIC Lombardia, this dual commitment contributes to building increasingly inclusive sports, school and social environments. The day dedicated to movement, play and inclusion will therefore also be the time when children meet Ciccio il Riccio and the content designed to explain celiac disease.

## TL;DR - HCAP aims to raise 3-3,5 million francs - The second round closes on October 22 - The fundraising is aimed at the fan base - Davide Mottis identifies financial stability as the objective
## Key facts - Company → Hockey Club Ambrì-Piotta - Authorized increase → 5 million francs - Target → 3-3,5 million, including the March round - Deadline → October 22 - Organizers → organized fan groups and blue-and-white support groups - Interviewee → Davide Mottis, president of Ambrì
On Saturday afternoon, organized fan groups and blue-and-white support groups launched a fundraiser to subscribe to the HCAP shares that remained available following the capital increase decided in March by the Leventine club.
### The second round aimed at the fan base
In the SEIDISERA interview on October 17, Ambrì president Davide Mottis ruled out the possibility that the mobilization indicated that the goal was still far away. His answer distinguishes between the significance of the two rounds. The March capital increase served a specific purpose and was aimed primarily at key shareholders; the current one, which closes on October 22, is instead aimed at the fan base.
Mottis explained that the new round arose from the need and the requests received from many fans who wanted to make a concrete contribution. Saturday's fundraiser is therefore linked to the request to involve all supporters in supporting HCAP. The president identified precisely this need as the reason for the second round.
In financial terms, the authorized capital increase amounts to 5 million francs. The target indicated by the president is an amount close to 3-3,5 million, including the March round. The figure was presented as an overall target, including the previous round.
In recent weeks, the club has pushed hard, including on social media, with various appeals to purchase shares. Mottis clarified that the insistence was intended to achieve the greatest possible success in the second round, despite a good response. He reported that the mobilization had received a strong response from fans and supporters. ### Financial stability as a priority
Mottis placed the fundraising within a broader project for Hockey Club Ambrì-Piotta. The president recalled that, ever since their election in February, they had identified two objectives: to regain some credibility and trust and to professionally reorganize HCAP.
The financial step is linked to the need to provide stability to the company in the medium to long term. Mottis's response linked the fundraising to a set of measures addressing the club's financial situation.
> The priority objective is to ensure the company's financial stability in the medium to long term.
HCAP, the president explained, still has certain outstanding debt obligations. These stem in particular from the construction of what Mottis described as a magnificent home. There are also still obligations toward the various mortgage lenders. Added to these is the liability arising from the loans that the club benefited from during Covid and that must be repaid.
For this reason, the capital increase is accompanied by various financial recovery measures and other measures that will be implemented in the coming months. Financial stabilization is the outcome management wants to achieve through this set of steps.
In the framework outlined in the interview, regaining credibility and trust, professional reorganization, and financial stability were identified as parts of the same path. The debt obligations and repayment of the Covid loans are the concrete elements cited to explain the financial priority. The capital fundraising thus becomes part of the medium- to long-term path described by the president. ### Expectations beyond the Gotthard
The next step mentioned in the interview concerns closing the capital increase, scheduled for October 22. Mottis said the club will take stock next week. Appeals in recent weeks, including through social media, accompanied the fundraising with the stated aim of achieving the greatest possible success in the second round.
The fundraising also had a dimension beyond the Gotthard. Asked about the presence of a representative from German-speaking Switzerland on the Board of Directors and possible investments from that part of Switzerland, Mottis answered affirmatively. He spoke of concrete and important signs of financial support arriving from the north of the Gotthard.
Among the elements mentioned was the event that also originated with the Donatoren-Club HCAP of the Canton of Uri. Participation was described as incredible, almost moving. For the president, it is a sign that something is moving in the right direction.
The club is looking to maintain this relationship. The expectations indicated by Mottis are twofold: to continue receiving support at the rink from fans and, above all, to open doors to possible commercial collaborations. The event was also seen as an opportunity to mend a rift that appears to have been healed.
The perspective outlined by the president therefore concerns more than support at the rink. Support from German-speaking Switzerland is also being considered for the commercial collaborations it can facilitate. Mottis reiterated that HCAP is not only a regional representative, but also an economic one. Next week's assessment will be the time indicated for taking stock of the second round.

### The concert at Malipiero
The Auditorium «Paolo Conti» of the Civic Music High School «Riccardo Malipiero» in Varese will host, on Saturday, October 31, «Due note… da paura», a concert by the Ensemble de Saxophones di Varese conducted by Giuseppina Levato. It begins at 20.30, for an event steeped in music and Halloween atmosphere.
The title of the event evokes a programme designed to link musical listening with evocative sounds. The programme will take the audience on a journey through famous pieces, keeping the different expressive possibilities of the saxophone family at its centre.
The Varese ensemble will therefore take centre stage in an evening in which the timbre of the saxophones and the variety of their registers play a specific role. The event description in fact highlights the ensemble’s ability to present well-known works in a different guise, through a programme designed to showcase the instrument family.
The venue is the Civic Music High School «Riccardo Malipiero» in Varese, with the Auditorium «Paolo Conti» designated as the concert space. The location and time are already set: Saturday, October 31 at 20.30. Giuseppina Levato will lead the Ensemble de Saxophones, identified as the concert’s conductor.
The evening is thus described as a musical event linked to the atmosphere of Halloween, but shaped by a varied programme and the expressive possibilities of the saxophones. The audience will be taken through famous pieces and evocative sounds, while the name «Due note… da paura» identifies the event hosted by the Varese music institute. ## The program featuring Orff, de Falla and Musorgskij
### A different guise for familiar works
The repertoire brings together works by Carl Orff, Manuel de Falla and Modest Musorgskij, alongside other compositions. As a whole, it is designed to move from solemn moments to more delicate passages, without giving up the evocative atmospheres.
The repertoire is described as a succession of different character types. Alongside the solemn moments, more delicate passages and evocative atmospheres have their place, according to a structure designed to accompany the audience throughout the evening. This alternation represents one of the elements indicated in the concert presentation.
A central role is entrusted to the ensemble’s transcriptions and arrangements. Familiar works from the musical repertoire will be heard in a different guise, connected to the possibilities of the Ensemble de Saxophones. The work for this formation highlights the timbre of the saxophones and makes it possible to bring out the variety of registers that make up the instrumental family.
The concert description insists precisely on this shift: not only celebrated pieces, but pieces reinterpreted through the sound of the saxophones. The transcriptions and arrangements make it possible to bring the recognizability of the selected works into the program and, at the same time, the specific timbral character of the ensemble. The musical journey thus remains linked to the three named composers and the other compositions selected for the evening.
The presence of Orff, de Falla and Musorgskij does not exhaust the announced repertoire. Other compositions complete a program built to alternate different characters, while arrangements highlight the saxophone family and its expressive possibilities. The indicated variety concerns both the musical works and the registers of the ensemble.
The combination of familiar repertoire, different registers and evocative sounds defines the event’s musical framework. The transcriptions and arrangements by the Ensemble de Saxophones will make it possible to hear familiar works in a different form, while maintaining the connection with the evocative atmospheres associated with the Halloween evening. ## The Ensemble and the meaning of the evening
### An event also designed for first-time attendees
For years, the Ensemble de Saxophones di Varese has worked to promote musical culture and showcase the saxophone repertoire. It is a commitment that defines the ensemble beyond any single concert and connects the event at Malipiero with the ensemble’s journey.
The ensemble’s work is in fact presented as a journey devoted to musical culture and the saxophone repertoire. The concert at the Auditorium «Paolo Conti» brings to the stage of the Civico Liceo Musicale «Riccardo Malipiero» a program in which conducting, transcriptions and arrangements are brought together around the saxophone family.
Giuseppina Levato will lead the performance of «Two notes… scary». Under her direction, the ensemble from Varese will present the program prepared for the occasion, in line with its commitment to promoting musical culture and showcasing the saxophone repertoire.
The project’s aim is to pair the quality of the concert with a format capable of engaging those approaching this type of ensemble for the first time. The event’s approach thus combines the quality of the performance with an openness toward those who have not yet had the opportunity to discover the Ensemble de Saxophones.
The event therefore brings together the ensemble’s musical work and its desire to engage new listeners. The evening keeps the saxophone repertoire as its central element, but is also presented as an occasion capable of guiding those approaching this ensemble for the first time. This is the meaning assigned to the format of «Two notes… scary».
The event is therefore on Saturday, October 31 at 20.30, at the Auditorium «Paolo Conti» of the Civico Liceo Musicale «Riccardo Malipiero» in Varese. This is where the Ensemble de Saxophones di Varese will present «Two notes… scary», with Giuseppina Levato conducting.

### The discovery at the construction site During the morning of Saturday, October 17, an active construction site in the industrial area of Arcisate uncovered military ordnance dating back to World War II. The item was found in the area affected by the activities, while work was underway.
Initial indications describe the object as a possible mortar bomb. The source in fact uses cautious wording: it would be a mortar bomb. The classification is presented as a hypothesis in the first report of what happened.
After the discovery, Local Police officers and Carabinieri personnel serving at the Arcisate Station arrived at the scene. Law enforcement cordoned off the area and made it safe. The intervention concerned the point where the artifact emerged and the surrounding space involved in the work.
The account of the incident thus focuses on three elements: the construction work underway, the presence of a remnant of war and the immediate response of law enforcement. The first element places the discovery in the industrial area; the second traces the ordnance back to World War II; the third explains the cordoning off and securing of the area.
The discovery took place in a specific area of Arcisate and not in a place indicated generically. The Local Police and the Carabinieri from the Arcisate Station are the operators who intervened at the scene, while the possible nature of a mortar bomb remains the description given for the artifact. The initial picture is therefore that of an area isolated after the ordnance emerged during the work. ## The history of the area ### The connection with the old powder magazine The location where the explosive ordnance emerged has an aspect that goes beyond the area's industrial function. A powder magazine once stood in the area, destroyed during World War II. The source connects the discovery to this history of the site and describes the old structure as the feature of particular historical interest associated with the area.
The destruction of the powder magazine itself may be connected to the emergence of the mortar bomb. The possibility that the ordnance was scattered as a result of the explosion that affected the structure during the conflict has not been ruled out. The possible connection is therefore built around two stages identified in the reconstruction: the explosion of the structure and the subsequent dispersal of the bomb.
The wording remains hypothetical. The source does not present the dispersal as an established fact, but links it to the fact that the powder magazine was destroyed during the war. The reference to the mortar bomb is likewise phrased cautiously, using the wording it is believed to be.
The site's historical value therefore arises from the overlap between the construction area and the place where the old powder magazine stood. The object emerged in an area noted for its particular historical interest, and this coincidence is why the discovery is also recounted from the perspective of local history.
The account provided does not yet attribute a definite origin to the bomb, but points to a possible connection with the events that affected the powder magazine. The explosion of the structure, its destruction during World War II, and the possible dispersal of the ordnance are the elements that make up the context of the incident.
The link between the area's past and the object's emergence during the work therefore remains the central point of the context: the old powder magazine was destroyed during the conflict, while the mortar bomb may have been scattered at that time. The source nevertheless presents the relationship between the two facts as conditional. ## The planned operations ### Removal, transfer and detonation The Prefecture of Varese and the relevant units of the Italian Army were informed of the incident. The technical follow-up to the discovery is therefore entrusted to the operations that will be carried out by the military personnel on the device.
The source indicates that the military personnel will handle the subsequent stages, from removal through transfer to a suitable location. Detonation can be carried out at that location under safe conditions. The sequence described does not stop at moving the object, but also includes the subsequent step planned for detonation.

The control continues pending the intervention of the specialists, to whom the operations indicated for managing the object are linked. The aftermath of the incident is marked by the shift from the control measures already in place to the operations entrusted to the military personnel. Their execution remains tied to the intervention of the assigned military personnel.

item.title: 2026 tax credit for border workers with children
item.description: Guide to the calculation and compilation of the EC framework for families of border workers: IRPEF 2026 rates and double taxation management.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland - 2026 IRPEF: 23% up to €28,000, 33% up to €50,000, 43% above - Tax credit managed via section CE of the 730 form - New Cross-Border Agreement in effect since January 1, 2024
## Key Facts - Cross-Border Agreement: in effect 01/01/2024 - IT Ratification: Law 83 of 13/06/2023 - 2026 IRPEF (brackets): 23% / 33% / 43% - Double Taxation Convention: 09/03/1976 - Allowance for new cross-border workers: €10,000 - Exemption for old cross-border workers: €7,500
The withholding tax on employment income for cross-border workers is deducted exclusively in Switzerland. To prevent the same income from being taxed twice, Italy applies the tax credit mechanism, which is technically managed through section CE of the tax return (730 form). This system allows for the recovery of the tax paid abroad against the tax due in Italy.
### The Regulatory Framework and the Cross-Border Agreement The current regime is governed by the New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and entered into force on January 1, 2024, following the Italian ratification via Law 83 of June 13, 2023. In parallel, the Convention for the elimination of double taxation between Italy and Switzerland, dating back to March 9, 1976, remains valid. It is important to remember that Switzerland is not a member of the European Union nor of the European Economic Area (EEA).
The distinction between worker categories is clear. Old cross-border workers, namely those who had already acquired this status before July 17, 2023, benefit from an exemption of €7,500 and a transitional regime that will extend from 2024 to 2033. Conversely, new cross-border workers are entitled to an allowance of €10,000. Both categories must correctly manage the tax credit to optimize the overall tax burden, especially in the presence of family dependents that influence the determination of taxable income in Italy. ## Tax Impact Analysis for Families The management of tax credits for a cross-border worker with children requires a careful analysis of the IRPEF rates planned for 2026. According to Law 199/2025 (art. 1 c. 3), IRPEF for the year 2026 will be structured with a rate of 23% for income up to €28,000, 33% for the bracket between €28,001 and €50,000, and 43% for income exceeding €50,000. This differs from the 2024-2025 income regime, where the rates were set at 23%, 35%, and 43%.
### Hypothetical Calculation Scenarios To understand how the tax credit operates, two hypothetical scenarios can be considered. In the first case, a cross-border worker with an average income and dependent children might find that the tax paid at source in Switzerland is higher or lower than the Italian IRPEF calculated on the same income. If the Swiss tax is higher, the tax credit cancels the tax due in Italy, but it does not generate a cash refund from the Agenzia delle Entrate for the exceeding amount.
In a second scenario, a cross-border worker with a high income (over €50,000) will be subject to the IRPEF rate of 43%. In this case, it is more likely that the tax due in Italy will exceed that withheld at source in Switzerland. The family will therefore have to pay the difference to the Italian treasury, despite the tax credit applied in the CE framework.
The final calculation is also influenced by the contributions paid in Switzerland, which include AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% borne by the employee, unemployment insurance (AD/AC) at 1.1% (with a cap of 148,200 CHF), and LPP professional providence, which varies between 7% and 18% based on the age bracket starting from 25 years. To these is added the LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%. ## Operating procedure for declaration To properly obtain the tax credit, the border worker must follow a strict procedure when filling in the Italian tax return. The main transaction takes place in the EC framework of the model 730, where the income produced in Switzerland and the taxes paid at source must be indicated.
### Compilation checklist - Recovery of Swiss salary certificates for the reference year. - Calculation of taxable income net of deductibles (€7,500 for old border workers, €10,000 for new ones). - Indication of the source tax paid to the cantonal tax administrations or to the AFC/ESTV. - Inclusion of data in the EC framework for the application of the tax credit. - Verification of deductions for dependent children provided for by Italian legislation.
It is essential that tax data is managed by the competent authorities: the AFC/ESTV at the federal level and the cantonal administrations at the local level. Bodies such as the FOPH/BAG or the Federal Statistical Office (BFS) have no competence in setting tax rates.
For those who also have to manage health insurance, border workers with a G permit have the right of option for LAMal, with deductibles for adults ranging between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500. Proper management of these costs, along with AVS and LPP contributions, is essential for sound family financial planning.
To simulate the impact of the new IRPEF 2026 rates on your net salary, you can use the calcolatore FISCALE.

## TL;DR

- When → this morning - Participants → parents, grandparents and citizens - Number → hundreds - Promoter → Comitato Como genitori a misura di famiglia - Starting point → piazzale Somaini - Route → lakeside promenade and city center - Reason → protest against the Rapinese administration's policy of shutting down dialogue
This morning, a stream of parents, grandparents and ordinary citizens crossed the lakeside promenade and city center for the #OraBasta demonstration. The initiative, promoted by the Comitato Como genitori a misura di famiglia, brought together hundreds of participants.
The protest stems from opposition to the Rapinese administration's policy of shutting down dialogue. The demand voiced along the route concerns greater attention to families and their needs. In the report, the mobilization is described as an occasion during which participants publicly reiterated their concerns, calling for consideration and listening from the administration as citizens.
The presence of parents, grandparents and ordinary citizens accompanied a demonstration focused on families' needs. The account also states that the initiative took place peacefully. The figure recorded so far is a turnout of hundreds of people, gathered to ask the administration for listening and attention. The starting point was piazzale Somaini, chosen, according to the report, not by chance. It is in the immediate vicinity of the Corridoni primary school, the subject of a long-running dispute between, on one side, parents and teachers and, on the other, the municipal administration.
The discussion involves parents and teachers on one side and the municipal administration on the other. The choice of starting point places the demonstration alongside the school matter mentioned by the source. The Comitato Como genitori a misura di famiglia began the mobilization near the primary school, before parents, grandparents and ordinary citizens crossed the lakeside promenade and the city center.
The connection between piazzale Somaini and the Corridoni is the local element that the report highlights alongside the protest against the Rapinese administration's policy of closing itself off to dialogue. The report thus places the reference to the school alongside the call for greater attention to families and their needs. Participation, described as peaceful, numbered in the hundreds. The report on the demonstration is marked as being updated. In the material available so far, the report provides a snapshot of a morning with hundreds of participants and a peaceful passage along the lakeside promenade and through the city center.
The message accompanying this presence is a request to be taken into consideration and listened to as citizens. The same mobilization calls for more attention to families and their needs and challenges the Rapinese administration's policy of closing itself off to dialogue. These are the elements that the Comitato Como genitori a misura di famiglia brought to the #OraBasta demonstration.
There is also the reference to the Corridoni primary school: piazzale Somaini is a stone's throw from the school, for which the text recalls a long-standing tug-of-war between parents and teachers on one side and the municipal administration on the other. The source does not indicate any other subsequent stages, but leaves the report on this morning's mobilization as ongoing.

item.title: Gornate Olona, the sports center remembers Kevin Palmieri
item.description: A plaque commemorates Kevin at Oratorio San Vito The child was 8 years old and disappeared in January 2024 Kevin loved playing soccer at the sports center
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A plaque commemorates Kevin at Oratorio San Vito - The child was 8 years old and went missing in January 2024 - Kevin loved playing soccer at the sports center - The family thanked the community of Gornate Olona
## Key facts - → Entrance place of the San Vito Oratory of Gornate Olona - Dedicated → by Kevin Palmieri - Age: 8 years old. - Disappeared in → January 2024, due to a sudden illness - → Football Passion
### The dedication at the entrance
A plaque dedicated to Kevin Palmieri was placed at the entrance of the sports centre of the San Vito Oratory in Gornate Olona. The name of the child, who died in January 2024 due to a sudden illness, is thus associated with the place where he loved to play football.
Kevin was eight. The structure of the oratory was for him a space linked to his passion for the ball: the source describes him as he ran happily behind a ball, expressing what the family calls his innate passion for football. The plaque was placed at the entrance of the sports centre, in a visible point outside the San Vito Oratory.
The text chosen to remember him recalls Kevin's smile and ties him to the dreams of every boy and girl. The images shown on the plaque are those of a rolling ball, a hug after a goal and the joy of being together. The message then carries the child's memory into the gestures and emotions that belong to the game.
The dedication is not just about the name engraved on the billboard. For the community of Gornate Olona, the entrance to the oratory is the place indicated by the family as the place where the heart of the community beats and where Kevin loved to play. The laying of the plaque makes that bond public and leaves his name in the sports centre linked to football.
The Palmieri family reacted with a message of thanks after installation. The text, disseminated on social media, expresses emotion at the fact that Kevin's memory remains right at the entrance of the San Vito Oratory. ### The family's message
After it was installed, the Palmieri family thanked people on social media for the plaque placed at the entrance of Oratorio San Vito in Gornate Olona. In the message, that place is presented as part of the family's history, and the initiative is linked both to the memory of Kevin and to the child's passion for soccer.
The Palmieri family wrote that the place was dear to them all, but especially to Kevin, who expressed his natural love of soccer there, joyfully chasing the ball.
In the text, the family explains that seeing the sign outside strengthens the feeling of belonging to the large family of the oratory. The plaque is described as a visible sign for those who enter and for the community that recognizes that place as special, because that was precisely where Kevin used to chase the ball.
The message of thanks continues by highlighting the location of the dedication. Knowing that Kevin's memory will remain etched at the entrance to the oratory, precisely where the heart of the community beats and where he loved to play, fills the family with deep emotion and gratitude. These are the two feelings expressed in the message that accompany the installation of the plaque.
Finally, the family thanks the sports club and all the people who made the gesture possible. The contribution is thus credited to the club and to those who helped create the dedication. The message describes the plaque as a special gesture and conveys the significance the initiative has taken on for the Palmieri family. ### The text of the dedication
The follow-up recounted by the source is linked to the message chosen for the plaque. The inscription looks to the future of the boys and girls and imagines Kevin's smile continuing to run alongside their dreams. Alongside the memory of the child who played football, the dedication therefore uses the language of play to speak of a presence that remains in the place.
The rolling ball is the first element evoked. Alongside it are the embrace after a goal and the joy of being together. These are images that the plaque places at the entrance to the Oratorio San Vito sports center, the same space the family associated with Kevin's innate passion for football. The dedication thus links the memory to the gestures and emotions listed in the message, without adding any other details about the child's life.
The chosen position makes the sentence part of the entrance to the oratory. Kevin's name and the words addressed to the youngest accompany entry into the place where the child loved to run after a ball. The source presents this permanence as a memory destined to remain etched precisely at the point where the heart of the community beats.
In the material reported, no other dates, initiatives or appointments linked to the dedication are indicated. The documented update is the plaque installed at the entrance and the message with which the Palmieri family thanked the community, the sports club and those who made the gesture possible. The follow-up thus remains entrusted to the public presence of the memory in the sports center of Gornate Olona.

item.description: New copper theft at the Tradate cemetery Several sheets stolen from the roof covering Water in the first-floor corridor Carabinieri investigations
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - New copper theft at Tradate cemetery - Several sheets stolen from the roof covering - Water in the first-floor corridor - Carabinieri investigations into the external cameras
## Key facts - Location → Tradate cemetery on the Varesina - Affected area → roof facing the market square - Consequences → damage and water infiltration - Investigations → Carabinieri and external video surveillance
### The inspection in Tradate
The new incident affected Tradate cemetery, overlooking the Varesina. The theft left part of the roof exposed, resulting in damage and water infiltration. The affected section is the one facing the market square, where the inspection established that several copper sheets had been removed.
Some citizens reported the situation after noticing water in the first-floor corridor, which had become slippery and potentially dangerous. The subsequent inspection established that the sheets had been removed and identified the affected part of the roof.
The reports thus led to the inspection: first, water was noticed in the passageway on the first floor, then several missing copper sheets were identified. The situation described therefore includes both the theft of the metal and the consequences for the roof and the indoor areas reached by the infiltrations.
In the corridor, the water had made the floor slippery. The same report revealed a possible danger for those passing through the first floor, while the inspection pinpointed the section of the roof facing the market square. For Tradate cemetery, the latest theft does not end with the removal of the copper. The roof was damaged and the water reached an indoor area of the cemetery. These are the immediate consequences reported in the reconstruction, together with the citizens' report that led to the situation being checked.
The new incident is therefore part of the scourge of copper thefts in the area's cemeteries. The inspection clarified what material was removed and the location of the section of roof involved; the rest of the reconstruction has been entrusted to the ongoing investigations. ## Not an isolated incident
The Tradate cemetery had already been targeted in the preceding days. On that occasion, the thieves had torn out gutters and downspouts from some chapels. Realizing that the material was not copper, they had abandoned it nearby.
### The other damaged structures
During that incursion, the marble part of a tomb was also damaged. According to the reconstruction, the structure may have been used to reach the roof coverings: the text maintains cautious wording on this point and speaks of a possibility.

The earlier incident and the new theft therefore involve different elements. In the case of the chapels, gutters and downspouts had been removed but left near the cemetery when it emerged that they were not copper. The succession of episodes draws attention to a phenomenon that, according to the source, continues to affect burial sites in the area. At Tradate, the damaged roof and water that entered the corridor add to the consequences described for this type of incursion. The presence of a damaged marble tomb also shows how the action affected elements other than the roof coverings. The local picture therefore includes roof coverings, gutters, downspouts, and tombs, with damage of different kinds. ## Ongoing investigations
Investigations into what happened are being conducted by the Carabinieri. The reconstruction remains to be verified and also includes the possible connection between the removal of the roof panels and the incident that had affected the chapels in the preceding days. It cannot be ruled out that the two incidents are connected, but the possible link will have to be verified.
### The possible connection
The two events are therefore being considered as part of the same reconstruction only as a hypothesis. Their possible examination falls within the still-open investigative phase, together with verification of the reconstruction and of any connection between the two incidents.
The further course of the affair is therefore tied to verification of the facts and of the possible link. What has already been established, however, is the damage to the roof, water infiltration, and the report of water in the corridor on the first floor. The new incident once again draws attention to the cemeteries in the area, where copper thefts can result in economic damage, restoration costs, inconvenience for visitors, and damage to structures and tombs.
In Tradate, the reconstruction remains entrusted to the investigations by the Carabinieri and to the possible use of the external images. Until the possible connection is verified, the two incidents remain separate in the reconstruction, while not ruling out a relationship between them.

item.description: AVS/AI 5.3%, AD/AC 1.1% and LAMal: what to check in the paycheck of a single border crossing in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%; AD/AC 1.1% - Elderly: exemption €7,500 in the 2024–2033 scheme - New frontier workers: deductible €10,000
## Key facts - Signing of the New Cross-border Workers Agreement → 23 December 2020 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Withholding tax on earned income → only in Switzerland - Convention against double taxation → 9 March 1976 - AD/AC → 1.1%, with cap CHF 148'200 - LPP → 7–18% by age group, from 25th year - Italian IRPEF 2026 → 23%, 33%, 43% - KVG → health insurance
On 1 January 2024, the New Cross-border Workers Agreement came into force, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. For the cross-border worker who checks his Swiss pay slip in the Canton of Ticino in 2026, this sequence is the starting point: the reference is not an agreement that came into force in 2026, but a regulation that is already operational.
The tax principle is clearly defined: the cross-border worker's income is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit to be indicated in the EC framework of 730. It is therefore not a double withholding tax on the same income. The Italy-Switzerland Convention on double taxation was signed on 9 March 1976; Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA.
To read the payslip as a single person, it is best to separate the tax part from the social items. Withholding tax rates, including federal and cantonal ones, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At the federal level, administration is the responsibility of AFC/ESTV; at the cantonal level, the cantonal tax administrations intervene. UFAS and BFS do not set these rates: the first concerns social security, AVS/AI, while the second collects statistical data.
### The dates that separate the regimes
The operational distinction concerns the date of 17 July 2023. Old cross-border workers, already cross-border workers before that day, have the exemption of €7,500 in the transitional regime 2024–2033. New cross-border commuters are included in the €10,000 exemption. The distinction precedes any reading of the net: before attributing a result to the condition of being single, one must place oneself in the correct category.
The Italian picture changes from 2026. For the Italian IRPEF three bands are indicated: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. For incomes 2024–2025 the reference remains 23%, 35%, 43%. The modification is referred to in Law 199/2025, article 1, paragraph 3.
Finally, the G permit, the AVS and the LPP enter into the pay slip control; for health coverage the correct term is KVG, i.e. health insurance, not "health tax". The new 2026 tax agreement must therefore be placed in the actual chronology: the New Cross-border Agreement operates from 1 January 2024. ## From gross to items that reduce net
The Swiss paycheck for 2026 cannot be interpreted with a single percentage. For a single cross-border commuter, the useful check is to combine the tax withholding with the contribution items and health coverage, without adding amounts that belong to different plans. The table collects the values ​​indicated for the employee or for the relevant contribution item.
### Two comparisons to make before looking at the net
| Voice | Indicated value | How to read it | |---|---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% employee | social contribution | | AD/AC | 1.1%, cap CHF 148'200 | contribution with indicated ceiling | | LAINF | 0.7–1.5% | indicated rate | | BVG | 7–18% by age group, from age 25 | data related to age | | KVG | right of option for cross-border workers G; adult deductibles CHF 300–2'500 | health insurance |
The first scenario concerns a cross-border worker who was already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023: in comparison with the new regime, the data to highlight is the exemption of €7,500, valid in the transitional period 2024–2033. The second concerns a new cross-border worker: the threshold to be compared is the deductible of €10,000. They are two different readings of the same pay slip and should not be merged into an average.
The IRPEF calendar must also be kept separate. From 2026 the bands indicated are 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000 and 43% above; for 2024–2025 they are 23%, 35%, 43%. These percentages describe the Italian situation and do not transform the Swiss withholding into a second income tax: the mechanism indicated remains the tax credit of the EC framework of 730.
For singles, the practical point is not to confuse the KVG item with the other deductions. A cross-border worker with a G permit has the right of option; the source also indicates deductibles for adults from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. The deductible should not be transcribed as a salary rate: it is the health parameter reported for health insurance.
The real net therefore emerges from the separate reading of tax, AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF, LPP and KVG, not from the use of an indistinct total. To transform this grid into a personalized salary estimate you can use calcolatore fiscale, keeping the Italian tax part separate from the Swiss one. ## Operational checklist for 2026
Paycheck verification does not require starting from a theoretical figure. It requires classifying each item and linking it to the correct regime. For single cross-border commuters, the following sequence helps to avoid confusing entry date, withholdings and health coverage.
### Five checks on the payslip
1. Identify the regime. Note if you were already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023. The answer addresses the comparison between the €7,500 exemption in the 2024–2033 transitional regime and the €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers.
2. Isolate the tax. Search for the withholding tax on earned income and check the principle applied: for cross-border workers it is only in Switzerland. For the Italian side, the tax credit passes through the EC framework of 730, so the control remains consistent with the rule against double taxation.
3. Read the contributions one at a time. AVS/AI/IPG is 5.3% dependent; AD/AC is 1.1% with cap CHF 148'200; UVG is 0.7–1.5%; LPP is 7–18% per age group from 25th year. Do not replace one entry with another.
4. Separate healthcare. KVG means health insurance. If you are a G cross-border commuter, consider the right of option and the adult deductible between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500. The healthcare item must be read separately from social security.
5. Attribute responsibility. For federal and cantonal rates, the administrative reference is AFC/ESTV at federal level and the cantonal tax administration at cantonal level. UFAS does not set tax rates and BFS collects statistical data.
This grid also avoids confusing the envelope entries with other references to cross-border work, such as refunds, INPS or the Brogeda crossing. None of these terms replace the AVS, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP rates, nor change the principle of withholding tax. The same caution applies to the new 2026 tax agreement: the date to be verified remains 1 January 2024, not 2026.
To estimate the real net, enter in the reading only the values actually available on the pay slip and apply the 2026 calendar to the Italian IRPEF: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. For a working estimate of net, use simulatore busta paga.

item.description: Best Film Winner: Ivan Markovic's Promised Spaces NGO Award for Effondrement of Anat Even Audience Award for Trop c 'est trop by Elisé
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Best Film Winner: Promised Spaces by Ivan Markovic - NGO Award assigned to Effondrement by Anat Even - Audience Award to Trop c'est trop by Elisé Sawasawa ## Key facts - Festival: Human Rights Film Festival Lugano - Winning work: Promised Spaces - Winning director: Ivan Markovic - NGO Award: Effondrement (Collapse) - NGO Award director: Anat Even - Audience Award: Trop c'est trop - Audience Award director: Elisé Sawasawa
The award ceremony of the Human Rights Film Festival Lugano has taken place, a prominent cultural event that saw the triumph of films committed to social, geopolitical and environmental themes. The main work that won the recognition as Best Film is 'Promised Spaces' by Ivan Markovic, a cinematographic work positioned halfway between fiction and documentary and set in contemporary Cambodia. The official jury that decreed the victory was composed of producer Gudula Meinzolt, active between Switzerland and Germany, film curator and programmer Dimitris Kerkinos, from Greece, and director Robin Petré, originally from Denmark. The jury expressed a detailed motivation to award the feature film, emphasizing how the work manages to create an extraordinary atmosphere of a dystopian society. The film addresses with great mastery the clash between different contexts and social classes, proposing itself as a hybrid work capable of inviting the viewer to a deep reflection on the current state of human relations, without imposing unambiguous or simplistic messages. The film also prompts consideration of how human action interferes with nature, transforming entire ecosystems into places rendered unrecognizable. The aspects of alienation that run through the entire visual narrative are further reinforced by a particularly careful and rigorous compositional and visual approach. For enthusiasts wishing to catch up on the viewing, the film is scheduled for a rerun at Cinema Iride. The cultural event continues to represent an important point of reference for the debate on human rights and major global issues within the Ticino city and regional context, attracting audiences and industry professionals from various regions and offering an international showcase for documentary and fiction cinema committed to addressing the most urgent and complex contemporary social issues. Alongside the main award assigned to Ivan Markovic, the jury and partner organizations of the festival have conferred other important official prizes that enrich the balance of this edition of the Lugano film event. The prestigious NGO Award was assigned to the work 'Effondrement' (Collapse), a film directed by Anat Even. Once again for this edition, the recognition was granted with the support and participation of Amnesty International Switzerland. The jury tasked with evaluating the works for this specific section was composed of Larissa Mettler, acting as co-president of the Executive Committee of Amnesty International Switzerland, alongside RSI journalist Moira Bubola and historian and journalist Jean-Marie Banderet. The official motivation released by the jury emphasizes how the voices and images within the film blend together in a way similar to the pieces of a puzzle, uniting different experiences and perspectives to bear witness to the moral collapse of a society at the moment when its own army carries out an action of systematic annihilation. The film was shot near the Gaza Strip after the date of October 7, 2023, capturing the remains of the kibbutz of Nir Oz, from which the population had been evacuated, and the destruction of the region beyond the border, with the aim of telling the story of the profound trauma generated by war and violence. A rerun screening is also scheduled for 'Effondrement' at Cinema Iride, thus offering a further viewing opportunity to the public interested in the international geopolitical and humanitarian themes addressed by the festival. The Lugano event also paid great attention to the feedback and direct participation of spectators, culminating in the awarding of the Audience Award. This recognition went to the work entitled 'Trop c 'est trop', a film made by director Elisé Sawasawa. The film focuses its attention and narrative on the ongoing armed conflict in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, documenting in particular the dramatic events related to the fall of Goma. The choice of the public confirms the sensitivity of the festival's spectators towards the humanitarian crises that are less told by the mainstream media but of dramatic global relevance. The programming of the Lugano Human Rights Film Festival is therefore confirmed as a central moment of cultural deepening, offering through screenings and debates with directors and experts a unique opportunity to discuss fundamental rights, the protection of natural ecosystems and the documentation of contemporary conflicts. The exhibition, through its different competitive and informative sections, continues to consolidate its role in the Ticino cultural scene, enhancing cinema as a tool for social investigation, historical testimony and promotion of civil and international awareness.

On Thursday evening, in Trevano, the Lugano Sharks won the Swiss Cup derby against Bissone, the home team led by Mihalov. The match ended at 25-14 and gave Federico Pagani the best possible start on the Lugano Sharks bench.
### Sharks night
Bissone sold their lives dearly before surrendering to their more esteemed opponents. The derby belongs to those challenges in which the difference in category traditionally struggles to emerge, because both teams face the match with particular passion or pressure. In Trevano this characteristic accompanied a game that remained open before the guests broke away.
The home team started in front, while the Sharks needed to gradually take control of the match. When Lugano imposed its greater experience and quality, the result began to shift in favor of Pagani's team. Bissone, however, had another jolt at the beginning of the third period, confirming the resistance shown in the match.
For Pagani it was the first official outing at the helm of the group. His debut as coach of the Lugano Sharks thus coincided with a victory in a Swiss Cup derby, at the end of a match in which Mihalov's team succumbed only after putting their opponents in the position of having to build the success during the match.
The 25-14 closed Trevano's evening and opened Pagani's adventure in the way described by the news: with a victory against Bissone and with an overall performance judged to be worthy of the commitment. The Swiss Cup now leaves room for the next appointment already indicated for the Sharks. ### The match changes gear
The first period saw Bissone slightly ahead. Mihalov's side therefore made a favorable start at home, while the Sharks had to wait until the next phase to take control of the contest. From that moment on, the Lugano team took charge of the match and made their greater experience and quality count.
| Phase | Progression | |---|---| | First period | Bissone slightly ahead | | Start of the third period | Surge from Mihalov's players | | Final phase | The Sharks finally pull away |
Bissone's reaction also came at the beginning of the third period. Mihalov's players had another surge, but the push was not enough to prevent their opponents from extending their lead. The final phase can be attributed to two elements evident in the reconstruction of the match: on the one hand, the tiredness of Bissone's most representative players, and on the other, the Sharks' bench, which was longer and more experienced.
The individual statistics gave a clear shape to Lugano's performance. On his first official appearance, Serbian newcomer Veljko Krstic immediately demonstrated his value, recording six goals. Right behind him was prolific scorer Alfano, with five goals.
However, the numbers of the two scorers do not tell the whole story of the evening. Coach Federico Pagani's team proved up to the task as a whole, managing the transition from the opening phase, which favored Bissone, to the part of the match in which the Sharks imposed their quality.
The match also marked Pagani's official debut after the change on the bench. The new coach took over from Jonathan Del Galdo, an experienced Genoese coach who had been in charge of the group for the last four seasons. The victory in Trevano thus marked the first official outing for both the new coach and the Serbian signing for Lugano. ### The next fixture
With the Swiss Cup challenge now behind them, the Sharks' schedule already features a new commitment. The Lugano team will return to the water tonight at the Lido pool, where they will host St. Gallen in the opening match of the Swiss Trophy.
The transition from Trevano to the Lido marks the change in venue indicated by recent events: moving from the derby against Bissone to the opening match of another tournament. St. Gallen will be the opponent in the first Swiss Trophy match, with the Sharks called upon to dive back into the action shortly after their victory in the Swiss Cup.
The competition has a specific characteristic. The Swiss Trophy is in fact a tournament dedicated solely to Swiss players or players who developed their athletic careers in our country. This definition distinguishes this upcoming commitment from the Cup match played in Trevano and clarifies the scope of the event.
For Lugano Sharks, the fixture at the Lido pool comes after Federico Pagani's official debut on the bench and the performance of new signing Veljko Krstic. The source presents the match against St. Gallen as the inaugural one, without indicating other tournament results or further stages of the calendar.
The next match will therefore be played at home, with Lugano called to host St. Gallen. The evening at the Lido completes the immediate aftermath of the Swiss Cup derby and brings the Sharks back into the water for the start of the Swiss Trophy, the tournament reserved for Swiss players or those who grew up athletically in the country.
