### Seventh place in the Three Valleys
With 913 points, Tre Valli Varesine achieved seventh place in the ProCyclingStats ranking, a portal specialized in evaluating races through a scoring system linked to the ranking of participants. The historic race in the Varese area thus confirms itself as a world-class event for professional cycling.
The placement emerges above all from the direct comparison with three competitions of international importance. Liège-Bastogne-Liège finished in eighth place, La Vuelta a España in ninth and Paris-Roubaix in eleventh. In the portal's ranking, therefore, the Lombard competition precedes all three: an order that brings the Varese race ahead of races indicated as monuments of the discipline.
The data concerns the historic race in the Varese area, presented by the source as a world-class event for professional cycling. Seventh place is accompanied by a precise score, 913 points, and by an equally precise comparison with the tests that follow in the list. The ranking thus compares the Tre Valli with the international events mentioned by the portal.
For the Lombardy competition, the heart of the news is the combination of placement and score. The race is seventh, while the three races mentioned are behind: Liège-Bastogne-Liège eighth, La Vuelta a España ninth and Paris-Roubaix eleventh. The comparison assigns the Tre Valli a higher position than those three competitions in the ProCyclingStats ranking.
The recognition, therefore, has a precise form: a seventh place obtained with 913 points, ahead of Liège-Bastogne-Liège, the Vuelta and Paris-Roubaix. The source presents this order as confirmation of the world level of the historic Varese race in professional cycling. ### The internal metric of the portal
The ranking drawn up by ProCyclingStats does not coincide with the official ranking of the International Cycling Union (UCI). To build the ranking, the portal applies an autonomous criterion that measures the overall strength of the runners at the start. The result of a competition therefore depends on the sum of the individual odds of the cyclists lined up at the start.
The calculation starts from the ranking of the individual athletes. The presence of a cyclist in the top ten in the world ranking is worth 50 points for the race. For subsequent positions, the score decreases progressively up to a point for athletes placed within the first thousand places. The sum of these odds produces the score assigned to the race and allows PCs to sort competitions based on the level of the group of starters.
It is this approach that gives technical meaning to the 913 points of the Tre Valli, without transforming them into a figure in the UCI ranking. The statistic measures the value of cyclists present at the start according to the scale of the portal; it is not presented by the source as the official ranking of international cycling.
At the top of the list, ahead of the Lombard competition, is the Tour de France, which leads with 1567 points. The top positions also include the World Road Championships, Lombardy, Milan-Sanremo, the Giro d 'Italia and the Tirreno-Adriatico. The list indicates the small group of tests that precedes the Tre Valli in the ProCyclingStats ranking and completes the numerical table of the ranking.
The score is then linked to the sum of the individual odds and the ranking band occupied by each athlete at the start. The internal metric of the portal translates the value of the group of starters into numbers according to the scale described by the source. The calendar and the local reaction The calendar of the Tre Valli Varesine decisively influences the success of the race. Its proximity to Il Lombardia leads top teams to field their captains in Varese. Participation allows them to refine their preparation and check their condition ahead of the Classic of the Dead Leaves. For the Varese race, therefore, the calendar position is linked to the possibility of having the captains of the top teams at the start. The source presents this proximity to Il Lombardia as an element that supports the success of the competition and leads the top teams to use Varese to fine-tune preparation and verify physical condition. The data also confirm the ongoing growth path of the competition. Two years after its last appearance in the Top 10, the Tre Valli Varesine has returned to the group of the world’s top ten races. The ranking figure is thus accompanied by a recent precedent of the same race, cited to describe its growth. The reference to the assessor’s words is the coincidence with the continental exhibition held in Ljubljana, Slovenia. After commenting on the European championship, Malerba added a clarification aimed at those who had raised objections about the presence of potholes along the route, considered dangerous for the athletes. The source therefore records, alongside the sporting recognition, also the local debate on the route and the calendar choice.

item.title: Construction sites in Lugano: the City Council aims to reduce inconvenience
item.description: The Municipality answers Michele Codella's question Work in Lugano will also continue in the coming years Focus between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Municipality answers Michele Codella's question - Work in Lugano will continue in the coming years - Focus between Botta Shelter and Corso Pestalozzi - The interventions in Molino Nuovo are close to completion
## Key facts - Question → Michele Codella - Construction works in progress → Besso and Genzana underpass - Project → StazLu - Future area → Botta shelter – Corso Pestalozzi - Road works → via Madonnetta, via la Santa and via Pazzalino - Subjects cited → AIL and Canton - Expected effect → contain time, costs and inconvenience - Recipients → citizens, users and economic activities
In Lugano, the Municipality responded to Michele Codella's question on construction sites that complicate the lives of citizens. The Executive has outlined the coordination of the work of the coming years and the ways to mitigate its impact on the population.
In recent years, Lugano has been affected by significant infrastructure works, which will continue in the future. The Municipality is therefore called upon to allow large construction sites to coexist with the interventions that the City cannot renounce, including road and infrastructural maintenance works connected to the credits intended for the extraordinary maintenance of the city roads and the canal network.
### The areas indicated by the Municipality
The StazLu project includes the construction sites underway in Besso and the Genzana underpass. In the coming years, the focus of the interventions will be the area between the Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi, where the Piazzale ex Scuole will be redeveloped, the tram-train network will be built and the underground infrastructure will be renewed.
Faced with the concentration of interventions, the Municipality aims to make the various clients collaborate. The intent is to avoid, as far as possible, that the construction sites follow each other separately, coordinate the different operational phases and limit the overall impact on citizens, users and economic activities. According to the Executive, this method should help reduce time, costs and inconvenience.
Extraordinary maintenance is also part of the planning: in the most demanding phases of large construction sites, the City intends to place work on roads and pipelines outside the Centre. It is with this in mind that the works were organized between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the roundabout of via Ruvigliana, along via Madonnetta, via la Santa and via Pazzalino. Now close to completion, they include the renewal of the underground infrastructure, carried out by the AIL, and the laying of the sound-absorbing asphalt, managed by the Canton. For those who reach Lugano for work, including cross-border commuters, the Municipality's response does not provide a timetable or an alternative route. The practical fact that emerges is another: the management of the works should focus on the sequence, so as to avoid maintenance arriving immediately after a large construction site or multiple interventions overlapping in the Centre.
It doesn't mean jobs are cancelled. The strategy described by the City tries to bring together different works: on the one hand the tram-train, the redevelopment of the former School Square and the underground infrastructures in the central area; on the other, the maintenance of the roads and the drainage network. For users, the expected benefit is not the absence of construction sites, but a reduction in overall impact, time and inconvenience.
### Before and after: the stated logic
| Situation to avoid | Choice indicated by the Municipality | |---|---| | Succession of separate construction sites | Coordination between different clients | | Maintenance superimposed on the most demanding phases in the Center | Programming outside the Center | | Molino Nuovo works contemporary with the large central construction sites | Advancement of interventions to limit the repercussions on traffic |
For a cross-border worker, this distinction helps to read the news without turning it into a calendar that the source does not provide. Besso and the Genzana underpass belong to the works already in progress; the area between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi is indicated as the main fire in the coming years; the interventions between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the via Ruvigliana roundabout are instead described as close to completion. These are three different situations and do not authorize us to deduce times, closures or diversions.
The answer puts citizens, users and economic activities on the same level. For this reason, planning does not only concern circulation, but also the impact on economic activities. The Municipality does not promise that every inconvenience will be eliminated: it indicates the objective of reducing it while the necessary works are carried out. To transform the answer into a useful reading grid for those who work in Lugano, the cross-border worker can follow a simple sequence, without attributing information to the source that it does not contain.
### Four operational steps
1. Identify the area. Distinguish between Besso and the Genzana underpass, where works are already underway as part of StazLu; the area between Pensilina Botta and Corso Pestalozzi, indicated for the next few years; and the stretch between Piazza Molino Nuovo and the Via Ruvigliana roundabout, where the works are close to completion.
2. Associate the intervention. For the central area, the municipal response refers to the Piazzale ex Scuole, the tram-train network and the renewal of the underground infrastructure. In Molino Nuovo, however, it indicates the renewal of the underground infrastructure entrusted to the AIL and the laying of the sound-absorbing asphalt by the Canton.
3. Read the sequence. The City will try to schedule extraordinary maintenance of roads and pipelines outside the Center during the most demanding phases of large construction sites. The works at Molino Nuovo were brought forward compared to the start of the large construction sites in the Center precisely to avoid overlaps.
4. Separate goal and result. Reducing inconvenience is the objective declared by the Municipality. However, the response does not quantify the effect on circulation and does not set a detailed timetable.
This procedure does not produce an itinerary, travel time, or detour. It helps you understand which phase your move concerns and so as not to confuse construction sites already underway, works planned in the coming years and interventions nearing completion. For those who travel through Lugano for work, including cross-border commuters, it is a more solid distinction than any route obtained by deduction.
If the reference is Molino Nuovo, the point to follow is the anticipation of the works compared to the Center. If the reference is the central area, the data to follow is the coordination between clients. If the reference is Besso or the Genzana underpass, the answer instead places them among the interventions already underway. In all cases, the Municipality links planning to the need to guarantee the works and reduce the impact on citizens, users and economic activities.
To combine this local reading with a work travel monitoring tool, consult the storico traffico e code ai valichi.

item.title: Cc-Ti Assembly: the economy is not the State's ATM
item.description: The Cc-Ti meets today in Bellinzona Gehri calls for healthy finances and a vision of the country Albertoni supports a stop to the increase in cantonal employees
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Cc-Ti meets today in Bellinzona - Gehri calls for healthy finances and a vision of the country - Albertoni supports the stop to the increase in cantonal employees - Albertoni rules out heavy cuts to services
## Key facts - Event: 109th assembly of the Cc-Ti - Location: Bellinzona - President: Andrea Gehri - Priorities: healthy finances, economy free to grow, trained young people and vision of the country - Initiative: Stop the increase in cantonal employees
At the 109th assembly of the Chamber of Commerce of the Canton of Ticino, held today in Bellinzona, the message was clear: Ticino must find its compass again and the economy cannot be called upon to pay the bill. Andrea Gehri, president of Cc-Ti, has indicated four priorities: restoring finances, encouraging economic growth, training young people ready for future challenges and promoting a vision of a country capable of uniting everyone, from right to left.
### Criticism of politics
Gehri did not name names, but criticized the political management. In his opinion, politics addresses the ordinary without governing the extraordinary.
> «Politics is managing the ordinary, but not the extraordinary».
In the president's message there is no mea culpa aimed at businesses. Companies, according to Gehri, work very quietly, they do not ask for subsidies and instead ask for framework conditions that allow them to prosper. The contested point is the withdrawal from the economy for decisions which, in its reading, do not fall within the economic competence.
The examples cited include the thirteenth AVS initiative and two initiatives relating to health insurance premiums. Gehri observed that in these cases money is spent without knowing where to get it first. It did not close the door to an intervention on revenues, if included in the symmetry of sacrifices. The proposal is to sit at the same table with politics, social partners and civil society: the Cc-Ti, he said, is available.
### Administration at the center
Director Luca Albertoni has broadened the picture. Doing business is more difficult not only in Ticino, but also in the context of the German crisis and American tariffs. Hence Cc-Ti's support for the Stop the increase in cantonal employees initiative, with the Chamber on the promoting committee.
Albertoni assured that heavy cuts to services are not needed. He calls for bringing the administration back to normal proportions, so that the state is effective for the citizens. Some tasks, he added, could pass to the private sector. But he said he doesn't believe there will be a bloodbath in the end: that's not the aim of the initiative. For those who live across the border and work in the Canton of Ticino, the connection with the assembly is real but indirect. The news talks about political directions, framework conditions for businesses and the size of the administration; does not communicate an immediate change to a paycheck, leave or benefit.
### The boundary between message and measurement
A cross-border worker can therefore read the text as a signal on the way in which the Cc-Ti would like to direct the debate, not as a new rule to be applied. The reference to the thirteenth AVS and to the initiatives on health insurance premiums remains a criticism of the procurement of resources. The source does not indicate amounts, deadlines, rates, documents or procedures.
The same applies to the initiative on cantonal employees. Albertoni speaks of an administration that needs to be brought back to normal proportions and admits that some tasks could pass to the private sector. However, it does not indicate which tasks, which services or which positions would be involved. He adds that he does not believe in a final bloodbath and specifies that that is not the aim. For a worker, therefore, the text does not allow anticipating a transfer, a reduction or a new hire.
For the cross-border worker, the second plan concerns personal issues that are not regulated here: G permit, AVS, LPP, KVG, refunds and withholding tax. The presence of the word AVS in the speech does not transform the meeting into a social security announcement; similarly, the reference to health insurance premiums does not define a KVG procedure. This distinction avoids confusing the debate on public spending with the rules of professional life across borders.
| Theme | Reported data | What doesn't appear | | Economy | Businesses demand framework conditions | An application measure is not indicated | | Administration | Some tasks may go private | No tasks or times are indicated | | Employment | Albertoni does not believe in a final bloodbath | There is no outcome indicated on the seats |
The prudent reading is this: the Cc-Ti asks for political direction, but the source does not yet describe a concrete change for the cross-border worker. To transform the message of the assembly into a useful reading, the cross-border worker can follow a simple sequence and not confuse the positions with the effects already in force.
### Four steps
1. Attribute each proposal. The general priorities and the call to the table with politics, social partners and civil society belong to Andrea Gehri's speech. The support for Stop the increase in cantonal employees and the evaluation of the tasks for the private sector are instead presented by Luca Albertoni.
2. Separate the proposal from the decision. The source reports Cc-Ti's support for the initiative, but does not report an outcome, an application date or a list of offices involved. Until these elements appear, the initiative cannot be read as a change that is already operational.
3. Isolate your personal theme. If the application concerns permit G, AVS, LPP, KVG, refunds or withholding tax, this meeting does not provide a new amount, a new deadline or a new procedure in the text reported. The reference to the thirteenth AVS and health insurance premiums should be left within the scope of the debate on public resources.
4. Look for the concrete fact. To understand if a political position really affects work in Ticino, it is necessary to wait for the possible indication of a service, of a task transferred to the private sector or of a decision on the framework conditions. The source does not attribute specific consequences to individual workers or categories.
### What remains today
The news therefore offers a reading grid, not a practice to present. The cross-border worker can distinguish the discussion on the economic direction of the Canton of Ticino from the rules of his own situation. There are no deadlines to meet or documents to deliver from the source.
The practical value of the distinction is to avoid attributing to Cc-Ti a decision that the source does not report. The positions are defined; the next step, however, is not described in the available text.
